info.title: Loop companion fleet protocol
info.description: Dedicated machine-to-machine JSON protocol. Available on non-preview companions only. Each request/response is limited to 4 MiB; the transport does not follow redirects, accept private DNS destinations, forward cookies or automatically repeat uncertain effects. Read the protocol-specific proof requirements on each operation.

post.description: Returns a signature over the supplied fresh nonce, confirmed origin and exact destination identity. No enrollment capability is needed. Browser Origin, Cookie, Authorization, CSRF, method-override and Sec-Fetch headers are refused. Host must match the serving companion's current HTTPS origin. Query strings and alternate path spellings are rejected.
post.x-loop-authentication: public challenge; credential challenges require an active grant context

post.description: Requires a nonce-bound machine signature. Current members may retrieve signed history from an enrolled replica without an access credential or controller connection. A new member may prove its admission with at most 1,024 signed entries and 768 KiB, connected to the receiver's current head; this read changes no grant. Removed members may retrieve only the chain ending at their recorded removal after proving their former key; later revisions and unrelated cursors are refused. Unanchored pages do not create trust. Browser Origin, Cookie, Authorization, CSRF, method-override and Sec-Fetch headers are refused. Host must match the serving companion's current HTTPS origin. Query strings and alternate path spellings are rejected.

Browser Origin, Cookie, Authorization, CSRF, method-override and Sec-Fetch headers are refused. Host must match the serving companion's current HTTPS origin. Query strings and alternate path spellings are rejected.

post.description: Relays a complete signed successor chain from this exact inactive enrollment operation's trusted checkpoint. Every edge must be authorized by the locally approved controller or its signed handoff. A relay need not occur in the earlier roster; it cannot install membership or grants. A verified removal cancels only the named operation durably, even if another ceremony reuses its grant. Exact packet receipts survive restart; completed enrollment is reported separately for ordinary synchronization. Browser Origin, Cookie, Authorization, CSRF, method-override and Sec-Fetch headers are refused. Host must match the serving companion's current HTTPS origin. Query strings and alternate path spellings are rejected.
